YMCA oF GREATER MONTREAL 


THE TIES THAT BIND 


You may have noticed that this issue of the annual report has 
appeared earlier than usual. It's not a mistake. We changed the 
dates of our fiscal year to coincide with the calendar year, 
so that this report on activities for the YMCA of Greater 
Montreal covers seven months rather than twelve, from June 1 
to December 31, 2006. In reviewing all our accomplishments 
during this short period, we realize that we worked twice as hard as usual! 


The strategic plan implemented in 2005 is already generating excellent results. We 
can safely say that we have now reached cruising speed and that over the last 
few months, we have successfully promoted and realized our community values 
on more than one occasion. 


In the past half-year, we increased the number and quality of our programs—be it 
for the youth leadership development project, our initiatives in elementary and 
high schools or the record number of participants at camp YMCA Kanawana. 
Incidentally, the camp is in the process of becoming an incredible YMCA dedicat- 
ed to outdoor and environmental education, which will serve as a model for youth 
and families. 


We have also been more thorough and at the same time more creative in design- 
ing and organizing our activities—an improvement duly noted by our funding 
agencies and development partners. As a result, our credibility and image are. fur- 
ther enhanced. 


The YMCA is performing better every year in its nine centres, its residence, its 
camp and its language school. In each location, we provide an environment that 
is increasingly welcoming, rewarding, better equipped and more modern. And, 
above all, we have created better synergy among the different teams, enabling us 
to set up more complementary and diversified activities and programs. We are 
pleased to see that Y participants are also more mobile within the larger network 
of YMCAs. 


In short, the ties that bind us to youth, families and communities are stronger than 
ever, as evidenced by the outstanding commitment of close to 3,000 staff members 
and volunteers, of hundreds of donors and of thousands of participants. On behalf of 
the Y and the values that inspire us, we thank each one from the bottom of our heart. 


Stéphane Vaillancourt 


Chair of the Board of Directors President and Chief Executive Officer 


Isa lasenza

Although this fiscal year was short, it was long on accomplish- 
ments! The year rounded out nicely with the startup of cons- 
truction work on the development project for camp YMCA 
Kanawana (described on page 6 of this report). Thus began 
@ Phase | of our ambitious vision: to share our exceptional 

550-acre site located near Saint-Sauveur with a greater num- 
These ties ber of youth and families, and to transform YMCA Kanawana into Quebec's first 
“green” outdoor and environmental education center. 


and these acts 


of generosity The development campaign is moving along well and by summer 2007, the new 
sanitary facilities will enable us to reduce our water consumption by 50%. 
Composting toilets—the first initiative of this scope in Quebec—will give campers 
enrich our lives. a unique opportunity for environmental education and awareness. 


and sharing 


With the support of the Foundation’s board of directors, numerous volunteers and 
donors, the Endowment Fund had reached $4.9 million by December 31, 2006. 
This growth resulted in increased investment revenues, enabling us to support a 
larger number of community development projects, such as Homework Help at 
the Pointe-Saint-Charles YMCA, Drug Prevention and Awareness at the West 
Island YMCA and “Wildlife Gaining Ground”, an environmental education program 
at YMCA Kanawana. 


In addition to all these efforts, dozens of volunteers participated in Community 
Support Campaigns organized in each of our nine centres. Their dynamic approach 
and dedication were rewarded, since we reached a new record for the third year 
in a row. 


These ties and these acts of generosity and sharing enrich our lives. Thank you to 
all those who support the Y and its Foundation by donating their time, energy and 


resources. 
Claude A. Garcia Michael Novak

YMCA KANAWANA DEVELOPMENT PROJECT 


THE PROJECT 


In the fall of 2005, we began dreaming of developing our camp YMCA 
Kanawana into Quebec’s first “green” camp—a year-round centre dedicated 
to outdoor and environmental education. 


A few months later, inspired by the Y’s vision, a multi-disciplinary team of 
professionals and stakeholders participated in a non-traditional integrated 
design process. We developed a unique and innovative camp concept that 
would reduce our ecological impact and foster a sense of environmental 
awareness and stewardship in its users and participants. 


YMCA Kanawana will include a 4-season eco-pavilion and 3-season installa- 
tions to welcome children, youth and families year-round. This project, a 
model of sustainable development, represents an investment of $4.4 million. 


In December 2006, we began the construction of 2 new sanitary installations which will include 16 toilets, sinks and 
showers each. These 3-season buildings will use natural light and ventilation and water will be heated by high-efficien- 
cy wood boilers that produce only trace emissions. Toilets will be composting - a first for Quebec camps - which will 
significantly reduce water and energy use. Campers will benefit and learn from these new installations this summer 2007! 


COMMUNITY OUTREACH - SHARING THE GIFT OF NATURE WITH THOSE WHO NEED IT THE MOST 


SUMMER 2006 

Since 2005, we have worked hard to make the Kanawana experience accessible to a more diverse population, through our 
9 YMCA Centers and community partners such as Toujours Ensemble, Batshaw Youth and Family Centres, the Centre com- 
munautaire de la Montérégie and the Municipality of Saint-Sauveur. Summer 2006 was a great success in this regard: 


* 12% of campers received financial assistance to go to camp, a threefold increase over 2004; 


* 28 children from the Pointe-Saint-Charles YMCA Homework Club kicked off their summer programming 
with 1 week at Kanawana; 


* all staff were trained in human rights and 40 Developmental Assets educational approaches; 


During changeover weekends, we also welcomed: 
* 10 low-income families referred to us by the Saint-Laurent CLSC; 
» refugee claimants from the YMCA Residence on a number of day trips; 
*a Class of Japanese children enrolled in an English immersion course at the YMCA Language School; 
* the Municipality of Saint-Sauveur's Day Camp Program for overnight trips and day outings; 


* 17 youth from the Saint-Michel neighbourhood in Montreal who are involved in C-Vert, a collaborative 
project with the Stephen Bronfman Foundation and TOHU (the Cité des arts du cirque); 


* 220 children from grades 3 and 4 at Ecole de la Vallée in Saint-Sauveur. 


These dozens of participants, all from diverse socio-economic and cultural backgrounds, were able to experience the great 
outdoors at YMCA Kanawana, in the environment of respect and understanding that are at the core of YMCA values. 


DEVELOPMENT CAMPAIGN 

A major capital’campaign is underway to realize this unique and innovative project. To contribute to the effort and find out more, 
you can visit the “About Kanawana” section at www.ymcakanawana.ca or contact Daniéle MacKinnon, Director of Financial 
Development for the YMCA of Greater Montreal at 514-849-5331, ext. 266 or at daniele.mackinnon@ymcamontreal.qc.ca. 


YMCA oF GREATER MONTREAL 


ENDOWMENT FUND 


20th ANNUAL HERITAGE CLUB DINNER 

On October 18, 2006, the Pointe-Saint-Charles YMCA provided a warm and welcoming venue for the 
20th Annual Heritage Club Dinner. More than 110 guests were on hand to hear participants’ stories 
and see the results of the Foundation’s efforts to increase its Endowment Fund. Since a campaign 
was launched in June 2004, the Foundation has received close to $800,000 in donations and 
commitments. The Fund has grown by more than 26%, increasing from $3.6 million to close to 
$4.9 million as at December 31, 2006. 


Michael Novak, Chair of the Foundation’s Board of Directors, and Foundation Governor John E. Cleghorn 
encouraged guests to contribute to this collective effort by making a current donation or by plan- 
ning a future gift in their will or through a life insurance policy. 


THOMAS S. GILLESPIE, RECIPIENT OF THE GABRIELLE AND MAURICE A. MASSE AWARD 
The award is presented every year to a person or couple who have made an outstanding contribution to the YMCA 
of Greater Montreal. This year, the award was presented to Thomas S. Gillespie. 


Mr. Gillespie is a longtime friend of the YMCA and his involvement exemplifies the organization's philosophy of 
holistic development in “spirit, mind and body”. In addition to attending physical fitness classes for more than 
three decades, Mr. Gillespie has also donated many hours of his time as a volunteer at the Downtown YMCA, as 
well as for the Montreal Association as a member of the Board of Directors of the YMCA of Greater Montreal and 
its Foundation. He has also been very active at the national level as a board member for YMCA Canada. 


On behalf of everyone at the YMCA, we wish to congratulate Mr. Gillespie and thank him for his exceptional 
dedication. 


PROJECTS SUPPORTED BY THE ENDOWMENT FUND 


The Endowment Fund provides a steady source of income for numerous community programs. A portion 
of the income (i.e., $57,016) was allocated to programs selected by donors, such as international 
development and camperships to YMCA Kanawana. The remaining balance of $51,255 was allocated to 
special projects selected by an Allocations Committee composed of volunteer members of the Board of 
Directors and YMCA staff. This year, six applications for funding were selected. 


Homework Help Pointe-Saint-Charles YMCA $17,500 
' Support for academic achievement for 7 to 12-year-olds 


Girls Basketball Du Parc YMCA $3,000 
Academic achievement and developing self-esteem through sport 


Drug Prevention and Awareness West Island YMCA $4,085 
Drug awareness and prevention in schools 


Breaking Seniors’ Isolation Guy-Favreau YMCA $11,670 
Social outreach with underprivileged and socially isolated seniors 


Wildlife Gaining Ground YMCA Kanawana $5,000 
Hands-on environmental education for campers 


Seniors on the Go Saint-Laurent YMCA $10,000 
Safe transportation service for seniors

YMCA oF GREATER MONTREAL 


YMCA HIGHLIGHTS 
JUNE TO DECEMBER 2006 


HEALTH, FITNESS AND RECREATION 


The Quebec Sports and Physical Activity Day was a great success: 300 participants discovered the 
YMCA Activaction® program and consulted with a certified trainer on site. 


Major renovations at the Pointe-Saint-Charles YMCA where the training room is now larger and 
better equipped. The centre achieved its three-year target membership goal after a mere six 
months thanks to this investment of nearly $230,000. 


A new SAM survey was conducted in 2006 throughout the YMCA Canada network to evaluate 
members’ satisfaction with their local Y. Some of our centres received top marks: the Hochelaga- 
Maisonneuve, Pointe-Saint-Charles, Saint-Laurent and Westmount YMCAs had grades of A or A+. 
The Guy-Favreau and West Island YMCAs received an honorable mention due to their marked 
improvement in certain service categories. 


The Du Parc YMCA’‘s Active Kids program launched in September was quite successful with some 
fifty participants attending each session. Active Kids offers various weekend activities to children 
aged 6-11, such as martial arts, yoga, dance, soccer and theatre. 


CHILD DEVELOPMENT 


The YMCA’s seven day camps founded on Y values remain as popular as ever. Despite fierce com- 
petition, income from the camps rose 4%. 


Furthermore, camp registrations at YMCA Kanawana were up 10% last summer. The camp also 
enjoyed record attendance by community groups for same-day outings. 


To help children and youth reach their full potential and become responsible adults, the YMCA 
produced a 2007 calendar for parents. The calendar contains useful information on the YMCA’s 
educational approach and the 40 developmental assets. 


Along the same lines, the Saint-Laurent YMCA developed a training program on the 40 assets 
to support parental skills development. Adapted to the realities of daily life, this very innovative 
project was highly praised by local partners. 


A record Community Support Campaign at the Westmount YMCA enabled 49 children with special 
needs to attend a day camp and participate in regular programs with the assistance of companions. 


COMMUNITY PROGRAMS 


Since last September, the Compensatory Work Program managed by the Downtown YMCA has 
been implemented in the Greater Quebec City area as well. Approximately 1,500 cases will be 
processed there, whereas the caseload for the Greater Montreal area will increase from 3,200 
cases to 4,000. 


In addition to improving its academic enrichment and support activities for students at the 
Champlain and Marguerite-Bourgeoys elementary schools, the Guy-Favreau YMCA formed a part- 
nership with the unique Jean-Baptiste Meilleur elementary school. 


Close to 20 dynamic youth between the ages of 12 an d16 who are involved in their community have 
participated in the Notre-Dame-de-Grace YMCA‘s Young Leaders program since last September. 


The West Island YMCA now has one single address. Since last fall, its community programs are all 
under the same roof, which creates a more dynamic, stimulating and better-structured environment. 


INTERNATIONAL PROGRAMS 


As part of the YMCA World Peace Week, youth from the Hochelaga-Maisonneuve YMCA organ- 
ized an intergenerational “improv” contest. Their improv team was pitted against the adults’ “Little 
League” team. 


The Covered Garden, a community program at the YMCA Residence, organized International 
Refugee Day in cooperation with, among others, the High Commissioner for Refugees and Amnesty 
International. The mission of the Covered Garden is to support new arrivals awaiting refugee status. 


INTERNATIONAL LANGUAGE SCHOOL 


A group of fifteen students aged 14-17 from the Hiroshima YMCA visited last summer on a language 
immersion trip. The Japanese youth had never been to Quebec before and they stayed at YMCA 
Kanawana as part of their trip. It was clearly a great experience for them, since they have already 
reserved for 2008. 


INNOVATION, RESEARCH AND 
DEVELOPMENT FUND 


In 2003-04, the YMCA of Greater Montreal created and fully funded the Innovation, Research and 
Development Fund to increase the reach of its programs and services. With resources of $50,000 
during the second quarter of 2006, the Fund supported the implementation of new initiatives, as 
well as projects aimed at maintaining the relevance, efficiency and quality of the YMCA’s actions. 
The projects selected meet strict criteria based on the YMCA’s mission and their level of integra- 
tion into the community. Projects are also subject to a year-end evaluation.
